hook: Zero to 650 mph in five seconds. Then only two parachutes opened.
narration: This capsule went from standing still to six hundred fifty miles an hour in five seconds.
It was Boeing's Starliner, in a pad abort test at White Sands, New Mexico.
Its four abort engines push forty thousand pounds, to pull a crew away from a failing rocket.
Then it pitched around, and the parachutes started pulling out.
[short pause] Only two of its three main parachutes opened.
Engineers build in backups for backups. Two good chutes still meant a stable ride down.
Next it dropped its heat shield, and airbags inflated underneath.
outcome: Starliner touched down safely on the desert floor, riding on two parachutes.

description:
Boeing's CST-100 Starliner fired its launch abort engines in a pad abort test at Launch Complex 32, White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico, on Nov. 4, 2019. Two of its three main parachutes opened and it touched down safely on the desert floor.
